documents.text:
{
  "title": "4D Drift Correction",
  "cn": {
    "func": "功能：去除**时间序列 3D 图像**在采集过程中产生的漂移（载物台爬移、热胀冷缩、样品沉降）。对每个时间点做强度投影,用**相位相关**估计它相对参考帧的位移,再把数据移回去：沿 z 投影得到横向 (x, y) 漂移,沿 y（或 x）投影得到轴向 (z) 漂移。参考帧可选**第一帧**（不累积误差）或**前一帧**（可跟踪大幅总漂移,累加得到总位移）。支持**亚体素精度**（默认十分之一体素）、漂移曲线平滑、样条插值位移或整体素位移（不插值、数值完全保留）。校正后的 4D 通道会作为新对象发布（**整数数据仍保持整数**,不会变成 float 而体积翻倍),并可导出漂移表（体素与世界单位、原始值与实际应用值）和曲线图。

第 2 页还能测量**两个通道之间的固定偏移**（色差或相机未对准）,可用标定片或数据本身测量,并把这个偏移应用到该通道的每个时间点。

本插件实现 **Fast4DReg** 的方法（Pylvänäinen 等,J Cell Sci 2023,https://github.com/CellMigrationLab/Fast4DReg）。**代码是独立实现的,不是移植**：该仓库同时附带 NanoJ-Core（GPL-3.0）,其漂移估计在历史上源自 NanoJ,而 GPL-3.0 与本插件的分发方式不兼容。相位相关本身是教科书方法。方法学请引用 Fast4DReg 论文。

第一个页签上的**一键执行全部步骤（按当前设置）**会无人值守地跑完流程：测量并校正漂移 → 保存漂移表与曲线图，每一步都使用你按下按钮那一刻各自页签上显示的设置。中间那一步——「用同一组漂移量校正另一个通道」——是复选框且**默认关闭**：它是针对同一会话的**独立工具**，而不是流程中的一环，后面的步骤不会用到它的结果，而且它会把整个运动图像序列重新读一遍并发布第二个通道。所有页签始终可以打开和修改参数，以便在运行**之前**逐页检查；某一步所需的输入尚不存在时，会在**它自己的按钮**上给出提示，说明缺的是哪一步，而不是把整个页签锁住不让进入。",
    "scenarios": "适用场景：活细胞长时间成像后每一帧都在缓慢平移,导致同一个细胞在不同时间点跑到不同位置,无法做追踪或强度统计；共聚焦/光片长时程采集中的轴向聚焦漂移；原位 CT 加载实验中样品的整体位移；以及多通道采集时两个相机（或两个波长）之间存在固定偏移,需要先对齐再做共定位分析。

用法提示：**先只估计、不发布**（取消勾选「发布校正后的通道」）看一眼漂移表和曲线,确认量级合理再正式跑。若漂移曲线在某几帧出现孤立跳变,通常是那几帧信噪比过低,可把「投影」改成最大值,或开启平滑。",
    "requirements": "环境需求：无需 GPU、无需联网、无需管理员权限,也不需要安装环境。全部在 Dragonfly 内部用自带的 numpy/scipy/scikit-image 运行。输入必须是**带时间轴的已发布 Channel**（至少 2 个时间点）；插件逐个时间点读取,因此内存占用约为两份体积。注意：校正会把数据移动,边缘因此出现空白（填 0）—— 这是不可避免的,原始数据没有那部分内容。"
  },
  "en": {
    "func": "What it does: removes drift that accumulated during acquisition of a TIME-LAPSE 3D image (stage creep, thermal expansion, settling). Each time point is reduced to intensity projections, the shift relative to a reference frame is estimated by PHASE CORRELATION, and the data is shifted back: the projection along z gives the lateral (x, y) drift, a projection along y (or x) gives the axial (z) drift. The reference can be the FIRST frame (no error accumulation) or the PREVIOUS frame (tracks large total drift, summed cumulatively). Supports SUB-VOXEL accuracy (a tenth of a voxel by default), drift-curve smoothing, and either spline shifting or whole-voxel shifting (no interpolation, every value preserved exactly). The corrected 4D channel is published as a new object - an INTEGER source stays integer rather than becoming float and doubling in size - and the drift table (voxels and world units, raw and as-applied) plus a plot can be exported.

Tab 2 also measures the CONSTANT offset between two channels (chromatic or camera misalignment), from a calibration slide or from the data itself, and can apply it to every time step of that channel.

This implements the METHOD of Fast4DReg (Pylvänäinen et al., J Cell Sci 2023, https://github.com/CellMigrationLab/Fast4DReg). The code is an INDEPENDENT implementation, not a port: that repository also ships NanoJ-Core (GPL-3.0) and its drift estimation historically derived from NanoJ, which is incompatible with how this plugin is distributed. Phase correlation itself is a textbook technique. Please cite Fast4DReg for the method.

**Execute All Steps with Current Settings** on the first tab runs the workflow unattended - measure and correct the drift, then save the drift table and plot - each step with whatever its own tab shows when you press it. The middle step, correcting a second channel with the same drift, is a tick box and is OFF by default: it is a separate tool over the same session rather than a link in the chain, nothing downstream consumes its result, and it re-reads the whole moving stack to publish a second channel. Every tab stays open at all times so the parameters can be read and changed BEFORE the run; a step whose input does not exist yet refuses at its own button and says which step is missing, instead of the tab being locked shut.",
    "scenarios": "Typical scenarios: a long live-cell acquisition where every frame has crept sideways, so the same cell sits at a different position in each time point and tracking or intensity statistics become meaningless; axial focus drift over a long confocal or light-sheet session; bulk specimen movement during an in-situ CT loading experiment; and multi-channel acquisitions where two cameras (or two wavelengths) have a fixed offset that must be removed before any colocalisation analysis.

Suggested workflow: ESTIMATE FIRST WITHOUT PUBLISHING (untick "Publish the corrected channel"), look at the drift table and the plot, and confirm the magnitude is plausible before committing. Isolated jumps in the drift curve usually mean those frames had poor signal - switch the projection to maximum, or enable smoothing.",
    "requirements": "Requirements: no GPU, no internet, no admin rights and nothing to install; everything runs inside Dragonfly on the bundled numpy/scipy/scikit-image. The input must be a PUBLISHED Channel WITH A TIME AXIS (at least 2 time steps); time points are read one at a time, so peak memory is roughly two copies of the volume. Note that correcting drift moves the data, so blank (zero-filled) margins appear at the edges - that is unavoidable, the original data simply has no content there."
  }
}
